generator.program.note: The zamias' own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the palm base: it gives the values its species leave unset, as Cycadaceae's program does.

generator.defaults.note: A ripe zamiad cone breaks up as its swelling seeds force its sporophylls apart, and only then do the seeds show and colour fully (Whitelock 2002, p. 20, 289). Whitelock gives no seed counts for these species; 24 show, about a small Zamia cone's (20 to 60 estimated; Lepidozamia has up to 360, p. 247), which genera with large cones raise.

appearance.note: A zamiad's female cone is a true cone of tightly packed sporophylls, closed over its seeds until it ripens and breaks up (Whitelock 2002, p. 18-20, 289): drawn closed, its faces flush.

traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Gymnosperms (DELTA, 2008 onwards, version of 5 August 2019), Zamiaceae: the leaflets have many parallel or wavy veins and no midrib (Stangeria aside).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: leaf division compound; read as "compound".

traits.vernation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: vernation circinate; read as "circinate".

traits.stipules.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: stipules present or absent, sometimes; read as {"true": "often", "false": "often"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: sexual system dioecious; read as "dioecious".

traits.division_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: division pattern pinnate (bipinnate in Bowenia), usually. Read together as {"pinnate": "usually"}.

traits.reproduction.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: reproduction cones; read as "cones".

traits.branching.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 145, 146, family Zamiaceae: branching unbranched or irregularly branched, usually; read as {"unbranched": "usually"}.

traits.ovule_bearing.note: Every cycad but Cycas bears its ovules in a true cone, two on the inner side of each sporophyll's face (Whitelock 2002, p. 18-19).
